quotes.quote: Lower Grocery Bills: We will scrap the PST on food production and farm equipment to lower the cost of B.C.-grown food.
True $10-a-Day Childcare: We will treat childcare as essential economic infrastructure to finally make the $10-a-day goal a reality for every family.
The government's refusal to course-correct will bury the next generation under a mountain of debt while failing to fix the affordability and safety crises.
CentreBC believes in responsible financial management-balancing the budget over the long term through smarter investments and spending.

cost-of-living-taxes.notes: Cut consumption taxes (PST on food production/farm equipment), make $10-a-day childcare real, balance the budget over the long term; no position on high-earner or corporate tax rates, no carbon-pricing revenue position.

quotes.quote: Housing You Can Afford: We must link housing policy to actual affordability outcomes rather than just counting units.
It means tackling the cost of living and housing affordability with real supply, not slogans.
Develop practical sector agreements in areas such as forestry, mining, energy, infrastructure, and housing that support both reconciliation and economic development.

housing.notes: No release or policy page is dedicated to housing. 'Real supply' and outcome-linked affordability only; nothing on zoning/density, rent control, social housing targets, or public land. Expect code:null on a housing question.

quotes.quote: Healthcare for Families: We will expand home care so seniors can age with dignity and reduce the paperwork for doctors so they can focus on seeing patients.
The waitlist for a long-term care bed has tripled since 2016, from about 2,400 people to over 7,200.
Accessible, well-funded healthcare and mental health supports.

health.notes: Strong critique (seniors/long-term care capacity, 're-paced' hospital projects, paperwork burden) with few commitments: expand home care, cut physician admin. No position on private delivery or pharmacare.

quotes.quote: an Indigenous participation framework, a dedicated B.C. Energy Future Fund, real safety and climate guardrails, guaranteed local jobs and procurement, and a clear legal pathway with full transparency.

We are committed to responsible economic growth, supporting small business, fostering innovation, and investing in green technology-while also championing our resource industries, including mining, forestry, and energy.
Why has a Provincial State of Emergency not been declared?

climate-environment.notes: Conditional support for new pipelines (five conditions, Oct 2025) plus unconditional championing of mining/forestry/energy and 'green technology'; no emissions target, carbon price position, or conservation commitment on the record.

quotes.quote: Create a single provincial framework for treaties and reconciliation agreements
Modern treaties have already demonstrated that negotiated agreements can create stability, strengthen Indigenous communities, and provide greater certainty for everyone.
Simply repealing DRIPA today would not undo those changes
When DRIPA was introduced in 2019, I was the only MLA who did not vote in favour of the legislation.
This failure to address the "Land Question" is our province's original sin

indigenous-reconciliation.notes: Most explicit commitments of any topic: single provincial treaties/reconciliation framework, sector agreements, finish modern-treaty negotiation, private-property coexistence. Leader states she was the only MLA to oppose DRIPA in 2019 and calls repeal pledges messaging.

quotes.quote: Establish an integrated FINTRAC-RCMP-CBSA cell in Surrey to map money flows, fast-track production orders and freeze assets within hours, not weeks.
set a 48-hour protection standard with real-time analytics to pre-empt sprees
Stronger Justice: Our public safety plan is backed by strong justice and treatment systems to ensure those who break the law face consequences while those with addictions get help.
it needs serious action with clear timelines, measurable milestones, meaningful tracking and transparent public accountability

public-safety.notes: Most developed file: 3-step extortion plan (FINTRAC-RCMP-CBSA cell, victim-first reporting + security micro-grants, dedicated prosecution track), enforcement-forward with treatment pairing, IPV accountability demands. No stance on bail specifics, sentencing minimums, or safe supply as distinct from treatment.
